guidanceConsulted.query: responsive reference documentation tables without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Lean on intrinsic sizing and the browser's layout engine; wrap potentially-wide content in overflow containers rather than masking with overflow:hidden; use overflow-wrap on unbreakable tokens; flex-wrap whenever overflow is possible; give replaced elements like iframe a block display value.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: every doc/compat table sits in .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto}; overflow-wrap:anywhere on h1, lede, code and table cells; <wbr> inside the long method H1s; .baseline-browsers is flex with wrap; pre blocks scroll internally; the embedded iframe is display:block with max-width:100%. Exception: no container queries - the shared single-column editorial measure fits the reference format (same as prior accepted pages).

guidanceConsulted.query: embedding third-party iframe demo lazy loading fallback
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Lazy-load iframes and media that are well outside the initial viewport (loading="lazy") so they never compete with critical rendering; keep non-critical third-party work off the critical path.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: the showcase demo iframe (far below the fold in the Examples section) carries loading="lazy" with explicit width/height to avoid layout shift; the two remaining concept demos are plain links rather than additional embeds so a single third-party document is loaded at most.

openQuestions: The draft WHATWG PR (#12590) names the attribute spellCheckDictionary while Chrome 153 ships spellCheckCustomDictionary, and the PR IDL writes [Exposed=Document] with no SecureContext while Chrome ships [Exposed=Window, SecureContext]. The page documents both verbatim and flags the divergence; when the PR is updated or merged the Syntax section and warn-block must be refreshed.

The 20,000-word and 128-byte limits are Chrome implementation values from the owners' Dev Trial instructions; the explainer deliberately leaves limits implementation-defined. If the limits change during the trial the two method pages need updating.

No Intent to Experiment thread exists on blink-dev for this feature as of 2026-09-13 - the dev trial was announced via a 'Ready for Developer Testing' post (linked) and the earlier Intent to Prototype used the working name 'Document Local Dictionary API'. If an Intent to Ship lands, add it.

Whether removeWords() of a word that is ALSO in the user's personal dictionary has zero effect (expected: yes, per the explainer's 'never affects underlying dictionaries') was not runtime-verified in this environment.
